component_findings.abi_calling_control: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: ABI/calling-convention/linkage choices are explicit or safely standardized for common interoperability cases. Evidence basis: Current Quidra documents explicit extern C declarations, FFI-specific diagnostics, a restricted ABI-safe scalar/string/bin/callback subset, reference restrictions and symbol-conflict checks; aggregate layout coverage and broader ABI/callback surface remain intentionally limited. Preserved paid evidence additionally records: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: ABI/calling-convention/linkage choices are explicit or safely standardized for common interoperability cases. Evidence basis: Current Quidra documents explicit extern C declarations, FFI-specific diagnostics, a restricted ABI-safe scalar/string/bin/callback subset, reference restrictions and symbol-conflict checks; aggregate layout coverage and broader ABI/callback surface remain intentionally limited. Preserved paid evidence additionally records: No FFI example program was available under the readable template paths; assessment is documentation-only against the frozen language spec. | No 'extern', 'ffi', 'foreign', 'cdecl', 'dlopen', or C-ABI declaration syntax appears anywhere in the documented surface language. | The 'Implementation scope' section explicitly enumerates what the native core currently supports (fixed-width numerics, casts, bin, arrays, tensors, image I/O, console I/O, namespaces, generics, classes, function values, bounded structured concurrency via task.all, atomic.Counter) and does not list any FFI/foreign-function/native-library-binding capability. | That same section names remaining development areas explicitly ('Cancellation, broader managed result transfer, self-hosting, broader signal-processing APIs, and broader package distribution') without naming general native interoperability as present or planned.…
